newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Thai sugar said unloading at China port.
newsitem.headline: Thai sugar said unloading at China port.

text.p: A 14,000-tonne cargo of Thai sugar was currently discharging in the south China port of Taishan, but whether the buyer had a valid import or tolling licence was questionable, a senior sugar trader in China said.
"The vessel has arrived in Taishan port. Now it has already begun discharging," the trader said, quoting port sources.
"It is definitely for tolling, but whether (the buyers) have the tolling licence, it's not so sure," he said.
Tolling involves importing raw sugar for processing and re-exporting.
Traders agreed that China is importing "a cargo here and a cargo there" for tolling but said they did not know which channels were being used.

A Hong Kong trader said, in another case, a vessel of raw sugar arrived in China but the buyer with a tolling licence demanded a much higher price, leaving the seller to look for another customer in Japan or South Korea.
Thai traders said a vessel called Jiang Chuan left for China on February 15 with 14,000 tonnes of sugar while the Marina Lauri, which carried 10,000 tonnes, left on March 7.
